Organisational Behaviour & Human Relations

Organisational behaviour and human relations — personality, perception, groups, communication, conflict and stress.

🎯 After this chapter you can

  • Describe organisational behaviour in nursing
  • Explain perception and personality in teams
  • Discuss group dynamics
  • Address conflict and communication

In simple words

Organisational behaviour studies how people behave in organisations. In nursing it explains why some teams work well and others conflict, and how the nurse administrator can support good relations.

Elements of organisational behaviour

Element Focus
Individual Personality, perception, learning, motivation
Group Role, norms, leadership, group decisions
Organisational Structure, culture, power, change

Groups in nursing

  • Types: formal wards, informal peer groups, committees
  • Norms: unwritten rules for acceptable behaviour
  • Roles: task roles and support roles; balance is needed
  • Group cohesion improves safety; fragmented groups miss information

Communication

  • Formal channel: duty lists, records, reports
  • Informal channel: personal conversations
  • Barriers: withholding facts, hierarchy, overload, cultural differences
  • Good communication reduces errors and improves morale

🔴 Human relations are a management tool

Warm, fair, clear communication reduces conflict, burnout and turnover. A unit in which staff can raise concerns without fear is a safer unit.

🔴 Most important for exams

  1. Organisational behaviour studies individual, group and organisational behaviour.
  2. Norms and roles govern behaviour in a unit.
  3. Group cohesion and clear channels improve safety.
  4. Conflict resolution uses facts, dialogue and fair process.
  5. Stress management protects both staff and patients.

⭐ Important for exams

  1. Perception and personality influence teamwork.
  2. The grapevine may spread rumours; open communication reduces it.
  3. Handover is a formal channel and is vital for safety.
  4. Role conflict is common in nursing.
  5. The administrator sets culture through example.

📌 Memory trick

Task and support roles: both are needed for a working ward.

60-second revision

  • Individual: personality, perception, learning, motivation.
  • Group: roles, norms, cohesion, decisions.
  • Communication: formal records and informal talk; avoid barriers.
  • Conflict: talk, facts, compromise, fairness.
  • Support and debrief staff to prevent burnout.

Test yourself

Role conflict occurs when:

Answer: A. Role conflict arises when conflicting expectations or demands fall on the same person.

Organisational behaviour studies:

Answer: B. It examines individual behaviour, group behaviour and the organisation as a whole.

Norms in a unit are:

Answer: B. Norms are informally shared expectations of behaviour that influence how staff act.

Barriers to communication include:

Answer: B. Hierarchy, overload and poor channels block accurate and timely communication.

Which improves morale most in a nursing unit?

Answer: B. Clear, fair and honest communication builds trust and morale.
